summary: Modern databases and data platforms have increasingly embedded AI/ML capabilities directly into the data layer, ranging from in-database model training (BigQuery ML, Redshift ML, Aurora ML) to managed LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, PostgreSQL pgai) and native vector search for retrieval-augmented generation. Vector search has become a critical enterprise AI primitive—adoption grew 377% year over year, the fastest among LLM-related technologies, and by 2026 roughly 75% of enterprise AI applications depend on vector search capabilities. The key architectural distinctions now lie in whether vector search is natively built in versus provided via extensions, and whether LLM access is managed (serverless functions) or requires external API integration.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (managed LLM and ML functions)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless, SQL-callable LLM functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER, CLASSIFY) backed by hosted foundation models (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Claude, Snowflake Arctic), plus Cortex Search for retrieval and Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL. Snowflake also extends these capabilities to Snowflake Postgres, letting Postgres workloads call Cortex AI functions.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and EMBED_TEXT for generating embeddings, and Cortex Search provides a managed hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval service built in.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated managed LLMs via Cortex functions; models hosted within Snowflake's governance boundary with no external API calls required. Supports Claude, Llama, Mistral, and Snowflake Arctic among others.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens processed per Cortex function; vector storage and compute billed under standard warehouse/storage pricing. No separate license for Cortex.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows creating, training, and running ML models using standard SQL (linear/logistic regression, boosted trees, k-means, time-series ARIMA, deep neural networks, AutoML). Via remote model integration with Vertex AI, it supports calling Gemini and other foundation models (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING) directly from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports vector embeddings storage and the VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) for approximate nearest neighbor search, plus ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING for embedding generation.
databases.llm_integration: Strong—remote models connect BigQuery to Vertex AI foundation models (Gemini, text-embedding models) and custom endpoints, enabling generative AI and embeddings via SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML priced by bytes processed (on-demand) or slot capacity (editions); generative/remote model inference and Vertex AI calls incur separate Vertex AI usage charges. Vector index storage billed as standard storage.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector adds a vector data type and similarity operators to PostgreSQL, enabling semantic search and RAG. pgai (by Timescale) adds SQL functions to generate embeddings and call LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama) directly, and pgvectorscale improves ANN index performance. These bring AI workflows close to operational relational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native-via-core-extension. pgvector is the de facto standard extension for Postgres vector search (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes); it is an open-source extension rather than built into vanilla Postgres, but is first-class in the Postgres ecosystem and bundled by most managed providers. Marked true because it is the canonical Postgres vector capability; on some managed services (e.g., Aurora) it is an add-on extension.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai extension—embeddings and LLM completions can be called from SQL against external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere) or local models via Ollama. Core Postgres itself has no built-in LLM access.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free to use; costs are from the underlying Postgres hosting (self-managed or managed service compute/storage) plus any external LLM API charges invoked by pgai.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL-based inference via Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models from SQL by integrating Aurora with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, and with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI/embeddings. Predictions are returned as part of query results, enabling inline sentiment analysis, predictions, and generative text without moving data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided only through the pgvector extension (a third-party/open-source extension), so native built-in vector search is not part of Aurora ML. Enable pgvector to perform ANN similarity search.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock (foundation models for text generation and embeddings) and SageMaker-hosted models, callable directly from SQL; also Amazon Comprehend for NLP tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora compute/storage plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend inference usage charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training and inference via SageMaker)
databases.description: Redshift ML uses the CREATE MODEL SQL command to train, deploy, and run ML models powered by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot, with support for bring-your-own-model and now generative AI via Amazon Bedrock/SageMaker JumpStart LLMs. Analysts build and apply models using familiar SQL on warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively supported as a dedicated ANN index service within Redshift ML. Redshift has added some vector/embedding support through integrations and functions, but it does not offer a mature built-in vector index comparable to dedicated vector databases; marked false for native dedicated vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Supports calling LLMs (text generation, embeddings) through integration with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and Amazon Bedrock models from SQL; core strength is predictive ML via SageMaker Autopilot.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML uses SageMaker for training (billed separately by SageMaker); prediction functions run within Redshift compute. Standard Redshift node/RPU charges plus SageMaker training/inference costs apply.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, RAG) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling—foundation model APIs, model fine-tuning, model serving, agent/RAG frameworks, and governance via Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated with the lakehouse that auto-syncs embeddings from Delta tables for retrieval and RAG.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a fully managed, built-in vector index that supports automatic embedding generation and sync from Delta tables, with hybrid keyword+vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Strong—Foundation Model APIs serve open and proprietary models (Llama, DBRX, Claude, etc.), supports fine-tuning, external model gateways, and agent frameworks, all governed by Unity Catalog.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving billed by compute/endpoint usage and tokens for foundation model APIs, on top of cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector search for operational data)
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and performing approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) similarity queries within the Atlas database, supporting RAG, semantic search, and hybrid search with filtering using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is built into Atlas via dedicated vector search indexes and the $vectorSearch operator; embeddings live alongside document data, eliminating a separate vector store.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs of its own, but integrates tightly with external models and frameworks (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas dedicated clusters; vector search runs on Search Nodes (separately scalable, billed by node size/compute) plus standard Atlas cluster storage and compute costs.
